newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jordanian soldier kills Israeli schoolgirls.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian soldier kills Israeli schoolgirls.

text.p: A Jordanian soldier shot dead seven Israeli schoolgirls on a fieldtrip on Thursday to a border site called "The Island of Peace", Israeli police said.
"We have a report of seven dead," a police announcement said. At least six were wounded.
Israel sent a helicopter and medical team to Jordan where some of the dead and wounded were taken.
The attack came amid a crisis in Middle East peacemaking between Israel and its Arab neighbours over plans to build a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called on Jordan to punish those responsible for "the murder of innocent girls".

The uniformed soldier turned his automatic rifle on the girls, aged about 13, as they looked from an observation point across the River Jordan to Syria and the Golan Heights. Other soldiers eventually overpowered him, witnesses said.

"We walked around and I heard shots...It was close...I turned around and saw a soldier taking a clip from his rifle and firing and we ran to the hill...He shot me in the hand," said Ornit, one of the 120 girls on an annual field trip from a school at Bet Shemesh near Jerusalem.
The girls were at a site called "The Island of Peace", a farm area that Israel leases from Jordan under their 1994 peace treaty.
Israeli officials said the shooting seemed to be the work of a lone soldier. They said they were in close contact with the Jordanian authorities who had sent investigators to the site.

"We yelled for the girls to get down and we all tried to hide," said witness Rosha Himi. "He came down and started chasing us. I saw how he inserted a new clip but with the second one he didn't manage to fire," Himi told reporters.

Apart from infiltrations by Palestinian guerrillas the heavily guarded Israeli-Jordanian frontier has been quiet for years. Israelis have been able to cross into Jordan since the 1994 treaty which gave Israel its warmest ties with any Arab state.

But ties with King Hussein have become icy since Netanyahu unveiled plans to build Jewish housing in East Jerusalem, which Palestinians say have plunged the whole U.S.-sponsored regional peace drive into crisis.
The king wrote to Netanyahu on Sunday accusing him of pushing Arabs and Israelis towards "an abyss of bloodshed and disaster".
"Perhaps the conclusion is that the King must hold his tongue so that a soldier doesn't take his words to mean more than he indended," Israel's Education Minister Zevulun Hammer told Army radio.

Hammer, whose pro-setttlement party has threatened to quit Netanyahu's coalition government if the Jerusalem building is frozen, said: "There is a problem with the best of our neighbours. Ninety percent of the Knesset voted for this peace and look what happens just for the heck of it. No one provoked here. There was no provocation."
The shooting puts pressure on Washington to defuse the crisis between Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat who has summoned Western and Arab envoys to a meeting in Gaza on Saturday.
Israel will not attend the meeting which Arafat has billed as an attempt to save the peace process.
